title: Isidore Havis died of natural causes despite being struck by rubber bullets: coroner
article: A provincial coroner has determined Isidore Havis, the 71-year-old man struck by rubber bullets during a standoff with police in Côte-St-Luc last year, died of natural causes because of his failing health before the incident.

"After analyzing all of the events I share fully in the opinion of the pathologist in the difficulty in establishing a causal link between the (injuries Havis suffered during the standoff) and his eventual death," Coroner Krystyna Pecko wrote in the conclusion of her report.
On July 30, 2013, Havis was armed with a revolver when he began to threaten Hydro-Québec installers while they tried to replace a meter on his property.

"His behaviour was aggressive and agitated," Pecko wrote. The threats touched off a standoff with the police who waited outside Havis's home on Guelph Ave. and tried to negotiate with him after he barricaded himself inside. After waiting 20 hours, the police stormed into the home using a battering ram.

"During this period, he suffered diverse injuries caused by, among other things, rubber projectiles fired by the police," the report states, adding Havis also likely fractured a hand earlier when he fell by accident.
Havis was taken to the Montreal General Hospital after being struck by at least two rubber bullets and died 18 days later, on Aug. 17, 2013.
When the police searched his home, they found 40 bayonets and 180 firearms inside.

Before he died, the Crown filed 14 criminal charges against Havis, while he was hospitalized, including one that alleged he tried to shoot a member of the Montreal police tactical intervention group who was part of the group that entered the home. Other charges alleged Havis assaulted, threatened and pointed a firearm at the Hydro-Québec installers.

During a previous confrontation with the police at the same home, in 2008, officers noted Havis appeared to be disoriented. According to the coroner's report, he suffered from "cognitive problems with possible elements of paranoia."

When he was taken to the hospital after the standoff, he was found to have suffered a fractured left arm, a fractured right elbow, a fractured hand as well as multiple contusions and abrasions on his face and abdomen. The fractured bones required surgery to repair.

Pecko determined the cause of death as natural and attributed it to an existing severe heart disease Havis suffered from "within the context of intense and prolonged stress." Havis had a pacemaker for his heart and was diabetic.

"The injuries incurred during the siege and the subsequent surgical interventions were contributing elements to the global context of the stress experienced by (Havis), but for a person in better health, even moderately, it wouldn't have caused the death of the victim," Pecko wrote.
